title: Get specific feedback from two stakeholders
why_matters: Vague feedback ("looks good") tells you nothing. Specific feedback ("section 4 is unclear about how we handle X") tells you what to fix. Asking for specific feedback is a skill; the wording you use changes what you get back. After this exercise you'll know what to ask, and the rhythm of how often.
steps: Pick two stakeholders who pre-read your BRD. Choose one who reads carefully and one who reacts more emotionally — both are useful, in different ways.
Book fifteen minutes with each. In the meeting, ask one question: "is there anything in the document you'd want to push back on, and why?".
Stay quiet after asking. Write down what they say verbatim where you can.
Send each a written summary of what they raised + what you'll do about it. Don't promise to fix anything you don't actually plan to fix.
success_criteria: Two short conversations have happened. You can name two specific things each stakeholder raised. Each has received a written summary with your response.
reflection_prompt: Whose feedback was harder to receive, and what was the part you wanted to argue with?
